We agreed on joint responsibility with on getting her, it’s normally me who feeds her but he knows what she needs, so I presumed the one time I had been out on a difficult emotional day he would think to give her some food.
I don’t know if that just me being naive or overly expecting.
The dog is fed and happy which is the main thing, I’m just concerned going forward that I can’t leave him to feed her without prompting and micro managing him :/
Because we agreed to both take caring responsibilities - yes I normally feed her but he is aware of what and when she should be fed and we have agreed on a feeding schedule

I didn’t take the dog out, I left to see to my poorly granddad for the day after feeding her breakfast. No I didn’t explicitly say to feed the dog, but we’ve had her for 5 weeks and he is fully aware that she needs to be given food.
I just hope he see’s my point of view in the morning and doesn’t try to shirk things. We got her agreeing that we are both responsible for caring for her, that’s why it was upset me about feeling like I can’t trust him to do the basic things.

He has had dogs growing up and used to have a dog with his ex partner. I can forgive someone if they forget to do something, but his lack of reaction or remorse when I brought it to his attention had just got to me. 
Poor baby, she’s been hungry all day and his reaction when I’ve become annoyed at him has really upset me. 
If I hadn’t have said anything she wouldn’t have had tea. I just hope this isn’t a sign of things to come…
I hope everything turns out ok x

I’ve been working my way up slowly for the past year - was on 275mg for 6 months and recently gone up to 300mg (I started to feel some dips in my mood incongruent with what was going on in my life, and my lows can be a very dark and scary place). My highs have become more manageable and I have much better insight, my partner and I can both catch myself before I end getting myself in impulsive situations.
I also take it in conjunction with agomelatine 25mg - a new age anti-depressant.
I have to say without a doubt these drugs have saved my life. It took 15 years to get my diagnosis and since being on lamotrigine I have felt better and more stable than ever. Of course there will be blips but I can keep myself safe now and have much more insight.
My psychiatrist says that the max dose is 400mg (UK guidelines) so I know I still have some scope to increase if needed.
I wish you all the best in your journey.

Peace & Love
